raw:
{
  "items": [
    {
      "category": "support_location_extent",
      "entity": "Full-height cantilever clamp",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1.1 calls the support the left boundary of a domain extending from x=-1 to x=1, but specifies Gamma_D at x=0. These are different support locations.",
      "readings": [
        "Clamp both displacement components on x=-1, -0.5<y<0.5.",
        "Follow the displayed Gamma_D literally and clamp the internal line x=0, retaining the full stated domain."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_extent_distribution",
      "entity": "Downward load at the right-edge midpoint",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1.1 calls this a point load at the center, but defines a finite loaded segment Gamma_N={1} times (-0.05,0.05). Eq. (3.16) treats t as a boundary traction.",
      "readings": [
        "A concentrated force at (1,0).",
        "A uniform downward traction over x=1, -0.05<y<0.05, spanning 10% of the domain height."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_magnitude",
      "entity": "Resultant of the right-edge load",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "The point-load wording and traction notation in Sec. 4.1.1 leave unclear whether the component -1 is a resultant force or a traction intensity. With the paper's fixed GL and volume-penalty weights, this normalization can also change the optimal layout; for pure compliance with a hard volume constraint, it would only scale compliance.",
      "readings": [
        "Total downward force 1; if distributed uniformly over the stated segment, use traction t_y=-10.",
        "Uniform traction t_y=-1 over the stated segment, giving total downward force 0.1 in the stated 2-D formulation."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "passive_region",
      "entity": "Material adjoining the clamp and loaded segment",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1.1 gives no passive-region mask or attachment-pad dimensions, and does not explicitly state whether support and load cells remain designable.",
      "readings": [
        "All cells are designable; there are no passive regions.",
        "Keep a one-cell-thick strip adjoining the clamp permanently solid.",
        "Keep a one-cell-thick pad adjoining the loaded segment permanently solid.",
        "Keep both the clamp strip and load pad permanently solid."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Initial volume-penalty coefficient",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Eq. (3.18) defines the penalty, but Sec. 4.1.2 specifies its initial coefficient only as order one. Table 2 supplies no exact initial value for case (a).",
      "readings": [
        "lambda_penal^(0)=0.5.",
        "lambda_penal^(0)=1.",
        "lambda_penal^(0)=2."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Upper limit of the volume-penalty ramp",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1.2 describes ramping the penalty to order 10^3–10^4, whereas Algorithm 1 repeatedly divides by 0.98 without specifying a cap. The stated range does not determine a stopping value or whether any cap exists.",
      "readings": [
        "Apply division by 0.98 at every outer iteration without a cap.",
        "Stop increasing the coefficient when it reaches 1000.",
        "Stop increasing the coefficient when it reaches 10000."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Timing of volume-penalty updates",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "The introductory text of Sec. 4 says the penalty is updated after each outer loop, but Algorithm 1 updates it before the state and topology stages.",
      "readings": [
        "Use lambda_penal^(0) during the first outer iteration and divide by 0.98 afterward.",
        "Divide lambda_penal^(0) by 0.98 before the first outer iteration's state and topology updates."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Reference cantilever Fourier bandwidths",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "Table 2 and Sec. 4.1.2 prescribe displacement bandwidth 35 and topology bandwidth 30. The spectral-bandwidth study in Sec. 4.1.4 identifies the reference case with these values reversed. These bandwidths restrict the represented fields and matter when matching the APF reference layout.",
      "readings": [
        "Topology bandwidth 30 and displacement bandwidth 35.",
        "Topology bandwidth 35 and displacement bandwidth 30."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "mesh",
      "entity": "Structured-grid analysis and design discretization",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1.3 gives a 120-by-60 FEM mesh, but does not specify element family/order, design-variable placement, or integration rules. The APF tensor-product sampling grid does not determine these FEM choices.",
      "readings": [
        "Use 120-by-60 bilinear quadrilateral displacement elements, cell-centered design variables, and finite differences for the GL gradient term.",
        "Use 120-by-60 bilinear quadrilaterals with continuous nodal displacement and phase fields, integrating the stated functionals by Gaussian quadrature.",
        "Split each of 120-by-60 rectangles into two linear triangles, with continuous piecewise-linear displacement and phase fields."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "FEM phase-field update scheme and pseudo-time step",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1.3 specifies 100 outer iterations and 20 phase-field updates per outer iteration, but delegates the semi-implicit scheme to unavailable reference [21]. The supplied text gives neither its pseudo-time step nor its explicit/implicit splitting and stabilization.",
      "readings": [
        "Implicit gradient term and explicit double-well force and compliance sensitivity, with pseudo-time step 0.001.",
        "The same splitting with pseudo-time step 0.01.",
        "A stabilized semi-implicit update with pseudo-time step 0.01 and an added linear stabilization coefficient of 1."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    }
  ]
}
